GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node identical to Toadpole.cs:69-86. Three MoveStates in a ring WHIRL -> SPIKEN -> SPIKE_SPIT -> WHIRL, plus a ConditionalBranchState 'INIT_MOVE' as the INITIAL state. Branch add order matches and it is observable -- ConditionalBranchState.GetNextState returns the FIRST branch whose condition evaluates > 0 (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54) -- so `AddState(WHIRL, () => !IsFront)` then `AddState(SPIKEN, () => IsFront)` must be, and is, mirrored by `add_state(whirl, lambda: not self.is_front)` then `add_state(spiken, lambda: self.is_front)` (toadpole.py:57-58). Because the initial state is a branch (not a MoveState), the machine's opening StateLog is EMPTY on both sides and the sticky-initial-move early return (seam step 30) does not fire, so the conditional really is evaluated for the first move. Executed (monster_probes_b04.py graphs).

guards.what: IsFront -> is_front, and where it is set
guards.rationale: ToadpolesWeak.GenerateMonsters (ToadpolesWeak.cs:15-26) mutates toadpole.IsFront = true and toadpole2.IsFront = false in that order; sim ToadpolesEncounter.create_monsters (toadpole.py:85-89) returns [Toadpole(is_front=True), Toadpole(is_front=False)]. The sim assigns self.is_front BEFORE super().__init__ (toadpole.py:40-41), which matters because MachineMonster.__init__ builds the machine and rolls immediately -- so the conditional reads the final value, as the game does (the game sets it before SetUpForCombat). Net: the front toad opens SPIKEN, the back toad WHIRL.

guards.what: SPIKE_SPIT spends the Thorns BEFORE the hits land
guards.rationale: Toadpole.cs:88-96 awaits PowerCmd.Apply<ThornsPower>(Creature, -SpikenAmount) and THEN the 3-hit attack; the sim does the same (toadpole.py:61-67) with an explicit comment. Order is observable: the toad's Thorns must be gone before the player's retaliation window.
Non-ascension, Toadpole.cs:49-55: SpikeSpitDamage 3, SpikeSpitRepeat 3, WhirlDamage 7, SpikenAmount 2. Sim toadpole.py:19-22 = 3 / 3 / 7 / 2. All match.

guards.what: no Monster.name class attribute on the sim port
guards.rationale: Toadpole is the only unit in this batch whose sim class sets no `name`, so the conformance driver falls back to the class name (`enemy_display_name`, conformance/combat_driver.py:37-44), giving "Toadpole". The game side is MonsterModel.Title, a localization lookup, i.e. presentation, and `name` is a sim-only tooling attribute with no C# behavioural counterpart -- so its absence is not a fidelity divergence (PROMPT.md v6 note 3's shape). Flagged in the batch report as a conformance-tooling nicety, not a gap. conformance/combat_driver.py is cited by name only, not hashed.
